incidents.title: AI-assisted AWS intrusion reaches admin in under 10 minutes
incidents.actor: Unnamed actor (Serbian-language comments in injected code)
incidents.targets: One AWS customer environment (RAG data buckets, Lambda, Bedrock)
incidents.outcome: Admin privileges in ~8 minutes, 19 AWS principals compromised, Bedrock models and GPU instances abused.
incidents.confidenceReason: Sysdig infers LLM use from code style, comments and hallucinated artifacts; no model is identified.
incidents.summary: Credentials from public S3 buckets led to Lambda code injection and rapid privilege escalation. Sysdig sees multiple signs that LLMs generated code and made real-time decisions. The attacker also invoked Bedrock models on the victim's bill.
incidents.quote: multiple indicators that suggest the threat actor leveraged large language models (LLMs) throughout the operation
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Sysdig has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

harness.note: LLM-driven operation inferred by Sysdig; no named harness

sources.title: AI-assisted cloud intrusion achieves admin access in 8 minutes

incidents.outcome: 46,812 subscriptions were cancelled; the teenager was arrested in July 2026.

incidents.title: VoidLink: advanced Linux cloud malware framework built almost entirely by AI
incidents.targets: Cloud workloads on AWS, GCP, Azure, Alibaba, Tencent; Docker/Kubernetes
models: TRAE SOLO (AI assistant in the TRAE IDE)
incidents.outcome: Framework with implants, rootkit evasion and dozens of plugins; first functional implant reportedly within a week; in-progress, not confirmed deployed at scale.
incidents.confidenceReason: Check Point 'believes' VoidLink was 'authored almost entirely by artificial intelligence, likely under the direction of a single individual'; basis is development artifacts. Also not shown deployed against a victim.
incidents.summary: Leaked TRAE-generated helper files showed one developer used spec-driven development with an AI assistant to produce a Zig-based C2 framework. Check Point called it the first well-documented advanced malware written mostly by AI.
incidents.quote: VoidLink’s development likely began in late November 2025, when its developer turned to TRAE SOLO, an AI assistant embedded in TRAE , an AI-centric IDE.

harness.note: TRAE SOLO wrote the malware, it did not run the attack; Check Point source shows Chinese-language planning docs
